boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Massachusetts Institute of Technology
boards.description: Ten current, under-21-safe food and grocery destinations with publicly listed evening or late-night availability in Cambridge.

cards.title: Maseeh Hall Late Night
cards.subtitle: 305 Memorial Dr, Cambridge, MA 02139
cards.notes: Check the academic-semester schedule before heading over; late-night service is listed Sunday through Thursday from 10pm to 1am.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus dining hall with a listed late-night meal period.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT lists Maseeh Hall late-night dining Sunday–Thursday from 10pm to 1am during the academic semester.
cards.access_notes: MIT lists late night 10pm–1am Sunday–Thursday during the academic semester; its page notes the location is closed for the summer season.

cards.title: Simmons Hall Late Night
cards.subtitle: 229 Vassar St, Cambridge, MA 02139
cards.notes: Use MIT’s dining-hours page to confirm service on your night; the listed late-night window runs Sunday through Thursday from 9pm to 1am.
cards.short_summary: An MIT residential dining stop with an earlier late-night start.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s dining terms list Simmons late-night service Sunday–Thursday from 9pm to 1am.
cards.access_notes: MIT lists late-night service 9pm–1am Sunday–Thursday, excluding the first meal-plan week, Institute holidays, and possible weather changes.

cards.title: Pinocchio’s After Class
cards.subtitle: 74 Winthrop St, Cambridge, MA 02138
cards.notes: Plan for Harvard Square and check the day: the shop lists 1am closing Monday through Saturday, with later Friday and Saturday hours in session.
cards.short_summary: A Harvard Square pizza-and-subs counter with hours extending past midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Pinocchio’s lists hours until 1am Monday–Saturday and until 2am on Friday and Saturday nights when students are in session.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: Sunday noon–midnight; Monday–Saturday 11am–1am; Friday and Saturday until 2am when students are in session September–May.

cards.title: Clover Central at Midnight
cards.subtitle: 496 Massachusetts Ave, Cambridge, MA 02139
cards.notes: Check Clover’s live schedule before leaving MIT; Central Square lists midnight closing Wednesday through Saturday and 11pm on several other nights.
cards.short_summary: A Central Square vegetarian counter with several midnight closings.
cards.evidence_claim: Clover’s Central Square location lists hours until midnight Wednesday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official schedule lists 10am–midnight Wednesday–Saturday, 10am–11pm Sunday, and 10am–11pm Monday–Tuesday; availability may change.

cards.title: Anna’s Davis Square Late Window
cards.subtitle: 236A Elm St, Somerville, MA 02144
cards.notes: For the latest listed option at Anna’s, make this a Friday or Saturday plan; the restaurant lists closing at 1:30am on those nights.
cards.short_summary: A Davis Square taqueria with late Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Anna’s Taqueria lists its Davis Square location open until 1:30am on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: Sunday–Thursday 10am–11:30pm; Friday and Saturday 10am–1:30am.

cards.title: Anna’s Porter Square
cards.subtitle: 822 Somerville Ave, Cambridge, MA 02143
cards.notes: Use the Porter Square stop when an 11pm close fits your plan; the official location page lists the address and current daily evening hours.
cards.short_summary: A Cambridge Anna’s location open every day into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Anna’s Taqueria lists its Porter Square location open every day from 10am to 11pm.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists daily hours of 10am–11pm and identifies the location beside Porter Square station.

cards.title: Toscanini’s First Street
cards.subtitle: 159 First St, Cambridge, MA 02142
cards.notes: Check the official location page before making the walk; it lists this First Street ice-cream shop open daily until 10pm.
cards.short_summary: A First Street ice-cream shop with a daily 10pm close.
cards.evidence_claim: Toscanini’s lists its 159 First Street location open Sunday through Saturday from noon to 10pm.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily hours of noon–10pm.

cards.title: Toscanini’s Central Square
cards.subtitle: 899 Main St, Cambridge, MA 02138
cards.notes: Use the Main Street location when Central Square is on your route; the official page lists daily service through 10pm.
cards.short_summary: Toscanini’s original Main Street shop, open nightly to 10pm.
cards.evidence_claim: Toscanini’s lists its 899 Main Street location open Sunday through Saturday from noon to 10pm.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists daily hours of noon–10pm.

cards.title: Prospect Street Grocery Stop
cards.subtitle: 115 Prospect St, Cambridge, MA 02139
cards.notes: For groceries or prepared items, confirm the store page before heading out; it lists the Prospect Street market open daily until 10pm.
cards.short_summary: A Central Square-area grocery stop with a listed 10pm close.
cards.evidence_claim: Whole Foods Market lists its Prospect Street store open daily from 8am to 10pm.
cards.source_title: Whole Foods Market Prospect Street Store
cards.access_notes: Official store page lists daily hours of 8am–10pm; prepared-food department hours can differ from store hours.

cards.title: River Street Grocery Stop
cards.subtitle: 340 River St, Cambridge, MA 02139
cards.notes: Use this market for a 10pm grocery run and check the store page for updates; the sandwich counter’s hours are listed separately.
cards.short_summary: A River Street market with a daily 10pm close.
cards.evidence_claim: Whole Foods Market lists its River Street store open daily from 8am to 10pm.
cards.source_title: Whole Foods Market River Street Store
cards.access_notes: Official store page lists daily hours of 8am–10pm; Market Sandwich is separately listed until 8pm.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named MIT spaces for studying, collaborating, gathering, and making campus life work between classes.

cards.title: Building 14 Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library outdoor seating
cards.notes: Use the outdoor seating for a reading break or a low-key meetup; the enclosed porch is a community space from spring through fall.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Hayden Library setting with seasonal community space.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries identifies the renovated Building 14 courtyard as having outdoor seating and an enclosed porch used as a community space in spring through fall.
cards.access_notes: Located at Hayden Library, 14S-100; review current library access policies before visiting.

cards.title: The Nexus
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library, 14S-130
cards.notes: Look for a community event or teaching session, or use the room as study space when it is not programmed for an event.
cards.short_summary: A Hayden room that shifts between events, teaching, and study.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries says The Nexus is used for community events and teaching and can also be a study space.
cards.access_notes: Map-listed at 14S-130 within Hayden Library; event use may affect availability.

cards.title: Collaborative Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library first floor
cards.notes: Bring a partner or project group: use flexible seating, whiteboards, and nearby library help for conversation-oriented work.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 collaborative first-floor reading room in Hayden.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries describes Hayden’s first-floor Collaborative Reading Room as a 24/7 space for current faculty, students, and staff with flexible seating and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: 24/7 access is for current MIT faculty, students, and staff; follow current library access policies.

cards.title: Hayden Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library floors 1 and 1M
cards.notes: Reserve a room when your group needs a monitor and writable planning surface; eight small-group rooms are available on floors 1 and 1M.
cards.short_summary: Reservable small-group rooms with monitors in Hayden.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries states that Hayden has eight group study rooms on floors 1 and 1M, with glass walls and large wall-mounted monitors.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; use MIT Libraries’ study-space reservation information for current availability.

cards.title: The Loft
cards.subtitle: Overlooking Hayden’s reading room
cards.notes: Set up a class meeting or study group in the collaborative area overlooking the reading room and café seating below.
cards.short_summary: An elevated collaborative area in renovated Hayden.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries says The Loft overlooks the reading room and café seating area and provides collaborative space for classes or study groups.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hayden Library; observe current library access and noise expectations.

cards.title: Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library second floor
cards.notes: Choose this quiet zone when you need independent reading or focused work, with views toward the Charles River and Boston skyline.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet reading zone on Hayden’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries identifies Hayden’s second-floor reading room as a quiet zone with views of the Boston skyline and Charles River.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hayden Library; keep conversation and calls elsewhere.

cards.title: East Study Room
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library, MIT ID access
cards.notes: Use the windows, varied seating, and docking stations for focused laptop work; bring an MIT ID for access to this room.
cards.short_summary: An MIT-ID study room with six monitor docking stations.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries describes the East Study Room as MIT-ID-access-only, with varied seating, windows, and six docking stations with 27-inch monitors.
cards.access_notes: MIT ID access only; confirm current building access before heading over.

cards.title: Barker’s Fifth-Floor Study Space
cards.subtitle: Barker Library, 10-500
cards.notes: Use the fifth-floor space for late independent or small-group work; the library says it remains available to anyone with an MIT ID.
cards.short_summary: A current MIT-ID 24/7 study option under the Great Dome.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries states that Barker Library’s fifth-floor 24/7 space remains available to anyone with an MIT ID.
cards.access_notes: MIT ID required; Barker’s stacks and service desk are closed as of March 30, 2026.

cards.title: Athena Lounge
cards.subtitle: Stratton Student Center, W20-575
cards.notes: Use this Student Center lounge as an individual or group study stop, then check the building’s current access rules before staying late.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Center lounge for individual and group study.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s Division of Student Life lists Athena Lounge (W20-575) among the Stratton Student Center’s individual and group study spaces.
cards.source_title: Student Center | MIT Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: Located in W20-575; building access can require card access outside general hours.

cards.title: Stratton Reading Rooms
cards.subtitle: Stratton Student Center, W20-540
cards.notes: Meet a classmate or settle into a study session in the Reading Rooms, then use the Student Center directory to find W20-540.
cards.short_summary: Named study rooms in MIT’s central student hub.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s Division of Student Life lists the Reading Rooms (W20-540) as versatile individual and group study spaces in the Stratton Student Center.
cards.source_title: Student Center | MIT Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: Located in W20-540; check current Student Center access rules before visiting.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Free MIT-community art, museum, library, and campus activities with clear access conditions.

cards.title: Browse the List galleries
cards.subtitle: Wiesner Building, 20 Ames Street
cards.notes: Meet at the Atrium-level galleries, look through the current exhibition together, then use the seating nearby to compare what caught your attention.
cards.short_summary: Contemporary-art exhibitions in MIT’s Wiesner Building.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT states that List Visual Arts Center galleries and programs are always free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Arts Access Supported by the Arts at MIT
cards.access_notes: Free and open to all; check the List’s current exhibition schedule before going.

cards.title: See student work at Wiesner
cards.subtitle: Stratton Student Center, W20-209
cards.notes: Drop into the second-floor gallery to view the current student exhibition, then use it as a low-key starting point for a Student Center meetup.
cards.short_summary: A gallery for MIT student art and design projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery’s official page identifies current exhibitions as free and open to the public with no reservations needed.
cards.access_notes: Free; no reservations needed. Public access hours may be restricted, so confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Explore the MIT Museum together
cards.subtitle: 314 Main Street, Cambridge
cards.notes: Bring an MIT ID and one guest, move through the exhibitions at your own pace, and leave time for the hands-on learning areas.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s science, technology, and art museum in Kendall Square.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT says MIT community members, including students, and one guest may visit the MIT Museum for free.
cards.source_title: Arts Access Supported by the Arts at MIT
cards.access_notes: Free for MIT students with ID plus one guest; standard admission applies outside that eligibility.

cards.title: Use the ICA university admission
cards.subtitle: 25 Harbor Shore Drive, Boston
cards.notes: Reserve the University Member timed-entry ticket under your own name, bring your MIT ID, and plan a gallery visit with classmates.
cards.short_summary: MIT-supported ICA admission for current students.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT states that current MIT students receive one free ICA admission per MIT ID through the University Member ticket process.
cards.source_title: Arts Access Supported by the Arts at MIT
cards.access_notes: A free timed-entry University Member ticket and MIT ID are required; one admission per MIT ID.

cards.title: Book a Gardner Museum visit
cards.subtitle: 25 Evans Way, Boston
cards.notes: Reserve an MIT-code timed ticket in advance, bring your MIT ID, and give yourselves time to move through the galleries and courtyard.
cards.short_summary: Free general admission for MIT students using the MIT code.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT states that current MIT students can reserve one free Gardner Museum admission per MIT ID using code “MIT.”
cards.source_title: Arts Access Supported by the Arts at MIT
cards.access_notes: Reserve the required free timed-entry ticket in advance with code “MIT” and present MIT ID.

cards.title: Pick up an MFA same-day ticket
cards.subtitle: 465 Huntington Avenue, Boston
cards.notes: Bring your MIT ID to the ticketing desk, collect the same-day ticket, and choose a few galleries to explore together rather than rushing the whole museum.
cards.short_summary: MIT-ID holders receive same-day MFA admission.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT states that an MIT Student or Employee ID receives a free same-day MFA general-admission or special-exhibition ticket.
cards.source_title: Arts Access Supported by the Arts at MIT
cards.access_notes: Present MIT ID at the MFA ticketing desk; the free ticket cannot be reserved online in advance.

cards.title: Enter the student art lending lottery
cards.subtitle: MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.notes: Watch for the annual lottery, enter if eligible, and visit the exhibition with friends to compare artworks before winners select a piece.
cards.short_summary: MIT students can borrow original collection art for an academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: The List Visual Arts Center states that the Student Lending Art Program is free for current MIT undergraduate and graduate students.
cards.source_title: 2026 Student Lending Art Program Exhibition and Lottery
cards.access_notes: Current MIT undergraduate and graduate students are eligible; participation and artwork distribution use the annual lottery process.

cards.title: Take a public-art walk
cards.subtitle: Across the MIT campus
cards.notes: Open the List interactive map, pick several works along a walkable route, and pause at each one to read the artist and location details.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided route through MIT’s campus art and architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT identifies an on-campus public art collection of more than 3,500 pieces and directs visitors to the List’s interactive map.
cards.access_notes: MIT’s campus public-art map is available to explore without an admission or purchase requirement.

cards.title: Settle into Hayden’s reading room
cards.subtitle: Building 14, 160 Memorial Drive
cards.notes: Use the quiet second-floor reading room for a shared reading session, then step into the courtyard or first-floor collaborative area to talk.
cards.short_summary: Library reading and collaboration spaces with river views.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries states that its resources are provided with free access and describes Hayden’s quiet reading room and study areas.
cards.access_notes: MIT students may use library study spaces; visitors’ access is limited to public entrance hours and library-use policies.

cards.title: Research something unusual together
cards.subtitle: 14N-118, 160 Memorial Drive
cards.notes: Choose a topic, request materials and book ahead, then meet in the reading room to examine rare or archival items side by side.
cards.short_summary: Appointment-based access to MIT’s rare and archival collections.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries states that the Distinctive Collections Reading Room is open to all, regardless of institutional affiliation, for use of its collections.
cards.source_title: Using the Reading Room | MIT Distinctive Collections
cards.access_notes: No admission or purchase is required; request materials and book an appointment at least six days in advance, then check in with photo ID.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct MIT study environments, with current library or Student Life access details and practical setup cues.

cards.title: Barker Library
cards.subtitle: Room 10-500, under the Great Dome
cards.notes: Bring your MIT ID for after-hours entry, then choose a quiet carrel, large table, or comfy seat; color printers and a KIC scanner are available.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, 24/7 MIT-ID study area beneath the Great Dome with individual and small-group options.
cards.evidence_claim: Barker’s fifth-floor study space is available 24/7 to MIT ID holders and offers quiet carrels, large tables, comfy seating, color printers, and a KIC scanner.
cards.access_notes: The stacks and service desk are closed; the fifth-floor 24/7 study space remains available to people with an MIT ID.

cards.title: E53 Study Space
cards.subtitle: E53-100
cards.notes: Set up at a study carrel when you need focus, or use the large table; bring a laptop to use the provided monitors and connector cables.
cards.short_summary: An ADA-accessible 24/7 room with 20 carrels, a large table, monitors, printing, and day lockers.
cards.evidence_claim: E53 Study Space seats 26, including 20 study carrels and one large table, and has monitors, laptop connector cables, color printing, day lockers, and 24/7 MIT-ID access.
cards.access_notes: MIT faculty, students, and staff may enter this 24/7 space with MIT ID when libraries are closed; the entire space is ADA accessible.

cards.title: Hayden Library
cards.subtitle: 14S-100, Humanities & Sciences
cards.notes: Use floors 1 and 1M for conversational work, then switch to the library’s quieter seating areas when you need a longer individual session.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 library study environment with 350 seats across conversational spaces and quieter work areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Hayden Library provides 350 study seats, conversational study spaces on floors 1 and 1M, computers, MIT-only printing, scanners, and 24/7 MIT-ID access.
cards.access_notes: Enter through the main or courtyard entrance with MIT ID when the libraries are closed.

cards.title: Hayden Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: First floor and first-floor mezzanine, Hayden Library
cards.notes: Reserve online for a group of two or more, check in with your MIT ID within 15 minutes, and use the screen, camera, speakers, and whiteboard.
cards.short_summary: Eight reservable rooms equipped for small group work and presentation practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Hayden has eight group study rooms for current MIT students, faculty, and staff; each includes a 55-inch LCD screen, laptop cable, camera, speakers, and large whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Current MIT community members may reserve rooms for up to three hours; groups of two or more have priority, and only Hayden rooms are available when libraries are closed.

cards.title: Rotch Library
cards.subtitle: Room 7-238, Architecture & Planning
cards.notes: Choose a seat by the large windows for focused work, and connect your laptop to an available monitor when you need a larger screen.
cards.short_summary: A bright, quiet 24/7 library room with more than 60 seats and laptop-ready monitors.
cards.evidence_claim: Rotch’s main floor is a quiet 24/7 study space with seating for more than 60 people, large windows, computers, monitors with laptop cables, MIT-only printing, and a scanner.
cards.access_notes: MIT faculty, students, and staff may access the 24/7 study space with MIT ID when libraries are closed; restrooms are in the nearby Infinite Corridor.

cards.title: Lewis Music Library
cards.subtitle: Room 14E-109
cards.notes: Check the day’s library hours before heading over, then use this music-focused library for course reading or research alongside its audio resources.
cards.short_summary: A music-library setting that combines study space with an Audio Lab and music collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis Music Library in room 14E-109 offers an Audio Lab and study spaces, but does not have 24/7 study space.
cards.access_notes: Not a 24/7 space; consult MIT Libraries’ current hours before visiting.

cards.title: The Nexus
cards.subtitle: 14S-130, Hayden Library
cards.notes: Use this named Hayden destination as a change-of-scene stop between library work sessions; confirm current building access before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A named study destination within the Hayden Library complex.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries lists The Nexus as a location in Hayden Library at room 14S-130.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hayden Library; building access follows current MIT Libraries access policies and hours.

cards.title: Athena Lounge
cards.subtitle: W20-575, Stratton Student Center
cards.notes: Bring individual work or a small collaboration to this fifth-floor lounge, and check Student Center access hours before planning an evening session.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Center lounge designated by MIT as a versatile individual and group study space.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT identifies Athena Lounge, W20-575, as one of the Stratton Student Center’s versatile individual and group study spaces.
cards.source_title: Student Center | MIT Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: The Student Center’s published summer general hours are 6 a.m.–7 p.m.; card access runs 7–11 p.m. Check the page for closures or schedule changes.

cards.title: Stratton Reading Rooms
cards.subtitle: W20-540, Stratton Student Center
cards.notes: Use the Reading Rooms when you want a dedicated Student Center setting for solo reading or collaborative work, and verify building hours before going.
cards.short_summary: Named Student Center rooms included in MIT’s individual and group study-space offering.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT identifies the Reading Rooms in W20-540 as part of the Stratton Student Center’s versatile individual and group study spaces.
cards.source_title: Student Center | MIT Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: The Student Center’s published summer general hours are 6 a.m.–7 p.m.; card access runs 7–11 p.m. Check the page for closures or schedule changes.

cards.title: Charles Vest Student Street
cards.subtitle: Ray and Maria Stata Center, Building 32
cards.notes: Use the café seating for a brief reading or laptop session between classes, keeping in mind that the area also supports tabling and small gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A Stata Center gathering corridor with café seating, display boards, and student-activity space.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT describes the Charles Vest Student Street in the Stata Center as a student-activity hub with display boards, student activity booths, and café seating.
cards.source_title: Event Spaces | MIT Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: This is an active gathering and event area, so availability may vary with tabling, small gatherings, or other scheduled use.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on streets at MIT’s edge, each with a documented reason to pause along the corridor.

cards.title: MIT Chapel: a timed quiet visit
cards.subtitle: Massachusetts Avenue corridor — 48 Massachusetts Avenue
cards.notes: Plan around the public visiting windows, then step inside to view Saarinen’s circular chapel and its skylight sculpture.
cards.short_summary: A non-denominational chapel with specific weekday public visiting windows.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT lists general-public visiting hours Monday–Friday, 10–11 a.m. and 1:30–2:30 p.m., unless a service is in progress.
cards.access_notes: General-public visiting hours are Monday–Friday, 10–11 a.m. and 1:30–2:30 p.m.; services can make it unavailable.

cards.title: MIT COOP at Stratton: campus books and supplies
cards.subtitle: Massachusetts Avenue corridor — 84 Massachusetts Avenue
cards.notes: Use the Stratton stop to browse MIT merchandise, textbooks, stationery, and other retail items during listed store hours.
cards.short_summary: A retail stop inside the Stratton Student Center area.
cards.evidence_claim: The COOP lists its MIT COOP at Stratton location at 84 Massachusetts Avenue and publishes weekday and Saturday hours.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Monday–Friday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; Saturday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed Sunday.

cards.title: MIT Museum: hands-on science and art exhibits
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 314 Main Street
cards.notes: Check the museum’s current ticketing and exhibition details before visiting the 314 Main Street galleries and program spaces.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s museum occupies the public-facing ground level at 314 Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT identifies 314 Main Street as the home of the MIT Museum and describes the building’s lobby as opening to the museum.
cards.source_title: Kendall Square at MIT — 314 Main Street and E28
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s official visitor information for current admission and gallery access.

cards.title: MIT Press Bookstore: browse publisher shelves
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 314 Main Street
cards.notes: Browse MIT Press titles and other books in the store at 314 Main Street; confirm the day’s schedule before making a trip.
cards.short_summary: The MIT Press’s Cambridge bookstore is in the E28 building.
cards.evidence_claim: The MIT Press Bookstore lists its location as 314 Main Street, Cambridge, and MIT’s directory lists weekday hours of 10 a.m.–6 p.m.
cards.access_notes: MIT’s office directory lists Monday–Friday hours of 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: MIT Welcome Center: maps, water, and a break
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 292 Main Street
cards.notes: Start here for a campus map, then use the listed visitor amenities before continuing through Kendall Square or onto campus.
cards.short_summary: A visitor-information stop beside Kendall/MIT station.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT says the Welcome Center at 292 Main Street provides campus maps, restrooms, water-bottle filling, free Wi-Fi, power outlets, and adjacent green space.
cards.access_notes: MIT lists hours as Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m., excluding MIT holidays and Institute closures.

cards.title: Koch Institute Public Galleries: biomedical images
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 500 Main Street
cards.notes: Enter during weekday gallery hours to explore current cancer-research displays, biomedical imagery, and the window-based exhibits outside.
cards.short_summary: Free public galleries connecting biomedical research with the Kendall community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Koch Institute says its Public Galleries present cancer-research projects and biomedical images, are open weekdays, and have Main Street-facing window exhibits.
cards.access_notes: Listed gallery hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m., excluding MIT holidays; window captions and QR codes can be viewed outside.

cards.title: Broad Discovery Center: free lobby exhibits
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 415 Main Street
cards.notes: Stop in to see the Discovery Center’s exhibits in the Broad Institute lobby, using MIT’s listed public-access times as a guide.
cards.short_summary: A free exhibit stop in the Broad Institute’s Main Street lobby.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT states that the Broad Discovery Center is in the lobby at 415 Main Street, has free exhibits, and is open to the public on listed weekdays and Saturdays.
cards.access_notes: MIT lists public access Monday–Friday 7 a.m.–7 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., excluding holidays and Institute closures.

cards.title: List Visual Arts Center: contemporary art
cards.subtitle: Ames Street corridor — 20 Ames Street
cards.notes: Visit the galleries for temporary exhibitions, then use the center’s public-art resources to continue looking for works across MIT.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s contemporary-art museum at the east edge of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The List Visual Arts Center says it is located at 20 Ames Street, presents temporary exhibitions and public art, and is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Visit — MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Listed gallery hours: Tuesday and Friday–Sunday 12–6 p.m.; Wednesday–Thursday 12–7 p.m.; closed Monday.

cards.title: Stata Center: Frank Gehry’s exterior
cards.subtitle: Vassar Street corridor — 32 Vassar Street
cards.notes: Approach from the Vassar Street side and take in the building’s layered, irregular exterior at the corner with Main Street.
cards.short_summary: A named MIT building housing CSAIL at the Main–Vassar corner.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT CSAIL identifies the Stata Center as a Frank Gehry-designed building at 32 Vassar Street, on the corner of Vassar and Main Streets.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies two Vassar Street entrances; access beyond public areas may be controlled.

cards.title: MIT Sailing Pavilion: Charles River waterfront
cards.subtitle: Memorial Drive corridor — 134 Memorial Drive
cards.notes: Use the pavilion’s posted directions to find the riverfront building across from Walker Memorial, then check MIT Sailing for program access.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s named sailing facility on Memorial Drive beside the Charles River.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Sailing lists the MIT Sailing Pavilion as Building 51 at 134 Memorial Drive, directly across from Walker Memorial.
cards.access_notes: MIT Sailing notes that Memorial Drive parking is difficult; review current program and access information before arranging a visit.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented MIT practices and recurring campus events, from measuring a bridge in Smoots to watching the sun line up with the Infinite Corridor.

cards.title: MIT Hacking
cards.subtitle: Benign practical-joke tradition
cards.notes: Explore the public MIT Hack Gallery to see documented examples; MIT describes hacks as elaborate, benign practical jokes rather than a program to imitate.
cards.short_summary: A campus tradition built around clever, anonymous, benign pranks.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Facts describes hacking as a distinctive MIT tradition of elaborate but benign practical jokes.
cards.access_notes: View documented public examples; do not attempt unauthorized installations or access.

cards.title: Count the Bridge in Smoots
cards.subtitle: Harvard Bridge measurement tradition
cards.notes: Walk the Harvard Bridge and look for the Smoot markings, the surviving result of a 1958 MIT fraternity pledge measurement.
cards.short_summary: A human-height unit of measure still marked on the bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Facts says the 1958 Harvard Bridge measurement in Oliver Smoot increments remains displayed on the bridge.
cards.access_notes: Use the public bridge walkway and observe markings without obstructing others.

cards.title: Earn a Pirate Certificate
cards.subtitle: MIT Physical Education tradition
cards.notes: If enrolled and interested, consult MIT Physical Education about the listed course requirements before planning a certificate path.
cards.short_summary: A faux-parchment certificate tied to a four-course physical-education sequence.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Facts states that completing archery, fencing, pistol or rifle, and sailing courses makes students eligible for an official Pirate Certificate.
cards.access_notes: Available only through supervised MIT physical-education courses; confirm current offerings and eligibility.

cards.title: The Brass Rat
cards.subtitle: MIT’s Standard Technology Ring
cards.notes: Look closely at a class ring’s class-specific details and beaver motif; current RingComm materials document the ring’s ongoing design tradition.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s class ring tradition began in 1929 and is designed anew by each class.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s 2026 RingComm says the Standard Technology Ring, known as the Brass Rat, began in spring 1929.
cards.access_notes: Ring ownership and ordering are limited to eligible classes; view the official gallery for documented designs.

cards.title: Keep the Ring Premiere Secret
cards.subtitle: Brass Rat reveal event
cards.notes: Eligible class members can follow their RingComm’s current announcements; the premiere reveal is intentionally kept from broad distribution.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial reveal that preserves the new class-ring design as a surprise.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s 2026 RingComm identifies Ring Premiere as an event it organizes and says its recording is withheld to preserve the premiere tradition.
cards.access_notes: Check the current class RingComm for eligibility, date, and venue.

cards.title: Ring Delivery
cards.subtitle: Brass Rat handoff ceremony
cards.notes: For an eligible class year, use the official RingComm delivery page for the current venue and pickup instructions after ordering.
cards.short_summary: The class-ring tradition includes a named delivery event after the design and order cycle.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s 2026 RingComm states that it organizes Ring Delivery and provides a dedicated delivery page with venue details.
cards.access_notes: Attendance and receipt require following the current RingComm’s eligibility and ordering process.

cards.title: MIT Mystery Hunt
cards.subtitle: January puzzlehunt competition
cards.notes: Follow the official hunt materials when the next January event is announced; teams solve linked puzzles leading toward a hidden coin.
cards.short_summary: A January puzzlehunt whose winning team writes the following year’s hunt.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Facts documents the MIT Mystery Hunt as a January puzzlehunt launched in 1981, with the winning team writing the next hunt.
cards.access_notes: Check the official hunt organizers’ current participation details before attending or joining a team.

cards.title: Pi Day Admissions Release
cards.subtitle: March 14 admissions tradition
cards.notes: Watch MIT Admissions’ official channels around March 14 for that cycle’s announcement rather than assuming a release time in advance.
cards.short_summary: MIT ties its regular-decision announcement to Pi Day and often nods to tau.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Facts says MIT typically releases admission decisions on Pi Day and frequently uses 6:28 p.m., colloquially Tau time.
cards.access_notes: Announcement timing can vary; rely on current MIT Admissions communications.

cards.title: MIThenge in the Infinite Corridor
cards.subtitle: Sunset alignment in MIT’s Infinite Corridor
cards.notes: In November or January, check MIT’s current notice and view the setting-sun alignment from the west end of Building 8.
cards.short_summary: Twice yearly, the setting sun aligns down MIT’s 251-meter Infinite Corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Facts calls the November and January Infinite Corridor sunset alignment an annual tradition known as MIThenge.
cards.access_notes: Timing depends on the sunset and weather; use public campus circulation areas and follow access guidance.

cards.title: Campus Preview Weekend
cards.subtitle: CPW for admitted MIT students
cards.notes: Admitted students can use CPW’s official information to choose from its programming and confirm the current year’s participation details.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s annual admitted-student weekend brings a dense schedule of campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Division of Student Life lists Campus Preview Weekend among its annual events and describes it as programming for admitted MIT students.
cards.source_title: Events — MIT Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: Intended for admitted MIT students; confirm invitation, registration, and schedule through CPW.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A self-guided first-weekend loop through MIT’s public-facing campus architecture, art, and museum spaces.

cards.title: Begin at Lobby 7
cards.subtitle: MIT main entrance, 77 Massachusetts Avenue
cards.notes: Start at MIT’s main entrance, then use the nearby Information Center or campus map to orient yourself before heading along the connected Main Group buildings.
cards.short_summary: A practical first landmark for getting oriented on MIT’s central campus.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT identifies 77 Massachusetts Avenue as its main entrance and places the Information Center in Room 7-121 inside that entrance.
cards.access_notes: The Information Center lists office hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday–Friday, excluding legal and Institute holidays; the exterior entrance remains a useful orientation point outside those hours.

cards.title: Walk the Infinite Corridor
cards.subtitle: Main Group buildings, MIT central campus
cards.notes: From Lobby 7, follow the interior corridor as far as public access permits and use the numbered-building signs to learn MIT’s campus layout.
cards.short_summary: A linear route through the core academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s visitor page identifies the Infinite Corridor as a place from which many departments, classrooms, and labs radiate; MIT also restored public access to it.
cards.access_notes: Stay in publicly accessible areas and follow posted building-access instructions.

cards.title: See a List Center exhibition
cards.subtitle: Wiesner Building (E15), 20 Ames Street
cards.notes: Head to the atrium level at 20 Ames Street and spend time with the current galleries; check the official page before leaving for the day’s exhibition schedule.
cards.short_summary: MIT’s contemporary-art museum provides a defined indoor cultural stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The List Visual Arts Center is in the Wiesner Building at 20 Ames Street, and the center states that it is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Visit | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: Tuesday 12–6 p.m.; Wednesday–Thursday 12–7 p.m.; Friday–Sunday 12–6 p.m.; closed Monday.

cards.title: Pause at Aesop’s Fables, II
cards.subtitle: Hockfield Court, Northeast Sector Lawn
cards.notes: Continue toward Hockfield Court and view Mark di Suvero’s painted-steel work from the surrounding lawn; keep clear of the sculpture and its supports.
cards.short_summary: A large outdoor sculpture beside the Stata Center.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT List identifies Aesop’s Fables, II as a 2005 painted-steel work installed at Hockfield Court near the Stata Center.
cards.source_title: Aesop's Fables, II, 2005 | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: View from the outdoor lawn and respect any on-site barriers or event setup.

cards.title: Circle the Stata Center exterior
cards.subtitle: Building 32, northeast MIT campus
cards.notes: Walk around the outdoor edges of Frank Gehry’s Building 32 and compare its brick, steel, aluminum, and brightly painted forms from different viewpoints.
cards.short_summary: A named MIT building with deliberately irregular, mixed-material architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT List identifies the Ray and Maria Stata Center as Frank Gehry’s 2004 Building 32 and describes its steel, brick, aluminum, and painted volumes.
cards.source_title: Ray and Maria Stata Center, 2004 | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Treat this as an exterior stop; enter only areas that are open to visitors.

cards.title: Visit the Sean Collier Memorial
cards.subtitle: Vassar Street entrance of the Stata Center
cards.notes: At the Vassar Street entrance, take a quiet moment to observe the granite memorial’s open central passage and read the site as a place of remembrance.
cards.short_summary: A named public memorial with a passage formed by interdependent granite blocks.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT List states that the Sean Collier Memorial, at the Stata Center’s Vassar Street entrance, was commissioned to honor Officer Sean Collier.
cards.source_title: Sean Collier Memorial, 2015 | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor memorial; maintain a respectful, quiet visit and do not climb on the structure.

cards.title: Study Kresge’s three-point roof
cards.subtitle: Building W16, west campus
cards.notes: Walk to Kresge’s lawn-side exterior and look for the copper roof pulling down at three points; view any performance only with a separately available ticket.
cards.short_summary: An Eero Saarinen auditorium known for its thin-shell roof geometry.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT List identifies Kresge Auditorium as Eero Saarinen’s 1955 Building W16 and describes its roof as an eighth segment of a sphere tied to the ground at three points.
cards.source_title: Kresge Auditorium, 1955 | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Use the exterior and lawn as the default visit; auditorium entry depends on building and event access.

cards.title: Find the MIT Chapel’s light well
cards.subtitle: Building W15, beside Kresge Auditorium
cards.notes: Cross the quadrangle to view the chapel’s cylindrical brick exterior and surrounding shallow moat; if the building is open, enter quietly and observe posted guidance.
cards.short_summary: A nondenominational Saarinen chapel designed as an intimate contrast to nearby campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT List identifies the MIT Chapel as Eero Saarinen’s 1954 Building W15 and describes its cylindrical form, shallow moat, and nondenominational purpose.
cards.source_title: MIT Chapel, 1954 | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is appropriate; interior access can vary with services, ceremonies, and building operations.

cards.title: Regroup at Stratton Student Center
cards.subtitle: Building W20, across from Kresge Auditorium
cards.notes: Use the exterior plaza as a waypoint, then enter only if open to visitors; notice the intersecting stairways and multipurpose layout described by MIT’s art center.
cards.short_summary: A named student-center building facing the Kresge and Chapel area.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT List identifies the Stratton Student Center as Building W20 across from Kresge Auditorium and MIT Chapel, with dining and large gathering spaces inside.
cards.source_title: Stratton Student Center, 1963 | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: Indoor access and dining availability may vary; use the exterior as a reliable stop and check posted entry information.

cards.title: Finish beside Baker House
cards.subtitle: Building W7, Memorial Drive by the Charles River
cards.notes: End with an exterior walk along Memorial Drive and look at Baker House’s curved river-facing form; respect that it is a residence hall and avoid residential entry.
cards.short_summary: A riverfront MIT residence hall designed by Alvar Aalto.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT List identifies Baker House as Alvar Aalto’s 1949 Building W7 and states that more than 90 percent of its student rooms look out onto the Charles River.
cards.source_title: Baker House, 1949 | MIT List Visual Arts Center
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas only; this is a student residence hall rather than a visitor interior.
